ab-roller: Loads the trunk at long length in the extended anti-extension position; genuine core demand above typical ab isolation work.
advanced-kettlebell-windmill: Overhead-loaded, standing hip hinge — genuinely high-skill despite the catalog's 'isolation' equipment tag; scored per true movement demand, not the label.
alternate-incline-dumbbell-curl: Incline position stretches biceps at long length at the bottom of the rep — Maeo/Pedrosa-line rationale for the elevated hypertrophy score despite being a simple isolation curl.
alternate-leg-diagonal-bound: High-impact single-leg bounding is a plyometric power drill, not a hypertrophy/strength tool; flagged for leg-day interference and knee/hip landing stress.
alternating-deltoid-raise: Sub-8-rep lateral raises stress the shoulder joint, per the rubric's own low-load high-rep design intent.
alternating-floor-press: Floor contact limits bottom ROM, reducing both stretch-position loading and shoulder stress versus a full bench press.
alternating-hang-clean: Hip-hinge explosive pull under a loaded implement — spinal_load and rep ceiling scored like a deadlift-family lift despite the kettlebell.
alternating-renegade-row: Plank-supported single-arm row demands real anti-rotation core control — complexity and joint_stress scored above a standard row for that reason.
anti-gravity-press: Diagonal landmine-style path — scored spinal_load below a straight standing overhead barbell press given the more shoulder-friendly angle.
archer-push-up: Bodyweight load shifts almost entirely to one arm — treated as unilateral despite both hands contacting the floor.
around-the-worlds: Full circular shoulder ROM under load is a legitimate impingement-risk movement despite the light weights typically used — auxiliary/prehab tool, not a hypertrophy cornerstone.
assisted-dip-machine: Assisted variant scored per the on-ramp rule — low focus scores despite still targeting triceps/chest directly.
assisted-pull-up-machine: Assisted variant scored per the on-ramp rule; the dead-hang bottom position still gives genuine long-length lat loading despite the machine assist.
atlas-stone-trainer: Rounded-back ground-up lifting technique is inherent to the movement — real lower_back stress even with good strongman form.
atlas-stones: Competition-weight version of the stone lift — scored fractionally above the trainer variant on strength given true maximal loading.
axle-deadlift: Thick-bar variant adds real grip/wrist demand on top of standard deadlift joint stress.
b-stance-rdl: Kickstand stance shifts most of the load to the working leg — scored as a genuine unilateral hip hinge with matching lengthened-bias hamstring loading.
back-flyes-with-bands: Band tension increases as the arms separate (band stretches most there), coinciding with rear-delt contraction rather than the lengthened start position — not a lengthened-bias movement despite using bands.
back-squat: Full-depth bottom position loads quads/glutes near their long length — counted as lengthened-bias per ROM-hypertrophy literature (deep squats outgrowing partial squats).
backward-drag: Distance/time-prescribed, not rep-prescribed, hence 0/0; backward mechanics create real eccentric quad loading — flagged for leg-day interference despite being a drag, not a run.
balance-board: Balance/proprioception tool, not a loading exercise — reps aren't the natural prescription unit, hence 0/0; the primary stressed joint (ankle) isn't in the tracked joint_stress list.
ball-leg-curl: Hip-extended bridge position keeps hamstrings relatively short at the hip throughout — unlike a seated (hip-flexed) leg curl, this variant is NOT a lengthened-bias exercise.
band-assisted-pull-up: Band assistance is greatest at the bottom (most band stretch), which blunts the dead-hang lengthened-position loading a true pull-up provides — opposite effect from the counterweight-assisted machine.
band-good-morning: Band tension peaks at the deepest hip-hinge (most-stretched hamstring) position — reinforces the lengthened-bias load.
band-good-morning-pull-through: Pull-through stance is generally gentler on the spine than a standing good morning, despite the shared hip-hinge pattern.
band-hip-adductions: Band tension peaks at the abducted (most-stretched adductor) starting position — a genuine lengthened-bias isolation movement.
band-skull-crusher: Upper arm stays roughly vertical, not overhead/shoulder-flexed, so this doesn't get the cross-joint long-head stretch that overhead triceps extensions do.
barbell-ab-rollout: Barbell loading allows progressive overload beyond a bodyweight ab wheel, with the same extended-position lengthened-bias core loading.
barbell-ab-rollout-on-knees: Kneeling stance reduces the lever arm versus a standing rollout — scored a notch lower on complexity/strength accordingly.
barbell-bulgarian-split-squat: Rear-foot-elevated stance increases bottom-position stretch on the front leg beyond a standard back squat — genuine lengthened-bias case, plus real barbell-on-back axial loading despite the unilateral stance.
barbell-curl: Straight-bar fixed grip is a well-known wrist-stress point relative to dumbbell or EZ-bar curl variants.
barbell-curls-lying-against-an-incline: Prone incline position drops the arms below the torso plane at the bottom — genuine stretch-loaded biceps position, similar mechanism to incline dumbbell curls.
barbell-floor-press: Truncated ROM (upper arm hits floor) avoids the stretched bottom shoulder position, making this a shoulder-friendlier press variant that emphasizes triceps lockout.
barbell-front-raise: Redundant deltoid stimulus given typical pressing volume; front delts are usually already well-trained.
barbell-full-squat: Full-depth ROM increases hypertrophy stimulus via greater length under tension but raises mobility/technical demand vs. standard-depth squat.
barbell-guillotine-bench-press: Wide elbow flare with bar path to the neck is a high-risk shoulder position; advanced/bodybuilding variant, reduce load vs. standard bench.
barbell-hack-squat: Grip/forearm fatigue and awkward bar position typically become the limiting factor before the quads; superseded by the hack squat machine or standard back squat.
barbell-hip-thrust: Best-supported glute hypertrophy exercise in EMG literature; a peak-contraction/shortened-range bias at lockout rather than a stretch-emphasis movement.
barbell-incline-shoulder-raise: Incline bench position lets the arm drop behind the torso plane, adding stretch-range ROM versus a standing front raise.
barbell-lunge: Bar-on-back position confers squat-like axial spinal load despite the unilateral leg action.
barbell-pullover: Classic stretch-position lat/chest exercise; shoulder position under load limits loadability for strength but is valued for the hypertrophy stretch stimulus.
barbell-rollout-from-bench: Bench start reduces ROM (easier regression of the standing ab-wheel rollout); still trains rectus abdominis/obliques at a lengthened, extended position.
barbell-shrug-behind-the-back: Behind-the-back bar position adds wrist/shoulder strain without a clear stimulus advantage over the standard barbell shrug (novelty is not value).
barbell-side-bend: Loaded standing lateral flexion under axial compression is a specifically flagged higher-risk pattern in spine biomechanics literature; light-load/high-rep only, if used at all.
barbell-side-split-squat: Frontal-plane loaded squat pattern demands more hip/groin mobility and balance than a standard sagittal-plane split squat or lunge.
barbell-squat-to-a-bench: Sitting-back box-squat pattern shifts load toward the hips/posterior chain and is often used to reduce knee stress versus a standard squat.
bear-crawl: Distance/time-based locomotion drill rather than a rep-based lift.
bear-crawl-sled-drags: Distance-based conditioning drag; continuous-tension loading (non-impact), unlike sled sprints.
behind-head-chest-stretch: Mobility/stretch entry, scored per convention: 0 across lifting goals, 0/0 rep window.
behind-neck-press: Behind-the-neck bar path requires excellent shoulder external rotation/mobility; flagged high-risk variant, most lifters better served by a standard front overhead press.
behind-the-neck-press-machine: Machine reduces stabilization demand vs. the free-weight version, but the impingement-risk shoulder position is inherent to the movement pattern, not the equipment.
behind-the-neck-pulldown: Flagged shoulder-impingement-risk variant; standard front pulldown achieves similar lat stimulus with less risk.
belt-squat: Load is transmitted through the hip belt rather than the spine — a genuinely spine-sparing alternative to back squats.
belt-squat-machine: Load is transmitted through the hip belt rather than the spine — a genuinely spine-sparing alternative to back squats.
bench-dip: Bottom position places the shoulder in a commonly flagged internally-rotated/extended stress position; often cautioned against for lifters with shoulder issues.
bench-dips: Bottom position places the shoulder in a commonly flagged internally-rotated/extended stress position; often cautioned against for lifters with shoulder issues.
bench-press-powerlifting: Competition arch/wide-grip technique shortens ROM (less hypertrophy stretch stimulus) but maximizes loadable weight — optimized for 1RM strength, not hypertrophy.
bench-press-with-bands: Bands shift the resistance curve toward lockout (ascending resistance), reducing tension at the stretched bottom — favors speed/lockout work over hypertrophy.
bench-press-with-chains: Chains create an ascending resistance curve similar to bands (more weight at lockout), though less extreme since the links still rest on the floor at the bottom.
bench-sprint: Plyometric/explosive drill; scored per the jump-work convention (high impact, leg-interference flag, low-rep prescription).
bent-arm-barbell-pullover: Classic stretch-position lat/chest exercise; shoulder position under load limits loadability for strength but is valued for the hypertrophy stretch stimulus.
bent-arm-dumbbell-pullover: Same stretch-position rationale as the barbell pullover; dumbbell allows a more natural shoulder path.
bent-over-dumbbell-rear-delt-raise-with-: Head-on-bench support removes the lower-back holding demand of the standard bent-over rear delt fly — the joint-friendlier variant.
bent-press: Old-time strongman full-body skill lift (lateral bend to press overhead); complexity matches or exceeds Olympic-lift-family demand — reserve for advanced/specialist populations.
bicep-curl-21s: Fixed 21-rep protocol (7 bottom-half + 7 top-half + 7 full reps); rep window reflects the defined technique rather than a flexible range.
bicycling: Outdoor riding requires balance, road awareness, and gear management, so complexity is scored above the stationary-bike version despite an identical physiological profile.
bird-dog: Bodyweight anti-rotation stability drill; negligible external loading keeps it low across all lifting goals despite its popularity as a corrective exercise.
board-press: Boards shorten the bench ROM for lockout-strength overload, which reduces stretch-position stimulus vs. full-ROM bench, so hypertrophy is scored below standard bench press despite heavy loadability.
bodyweight-flyes: Equipment tag ('ez-bar') looks mismatched with the name/pattern; scored as a bodyweight suspension-style fly per the name and push_horizontal pattern.
bosu-ball-cable-crunch-with-side-bends: Niche instability-plus-cable combo that duplicates standard cable crunch/side-bend value at higher complexity and setup cost, so scored below the simpler cable ab work.
bottoms-up-clean-from-the-hang-position: Advanced grip/stability drill — the bottoms-up hold forces very light loads, capping strength/hypertrophy value despite the explosive clean pattern; complexity rated at the top of the scale given the technical wrist-stability demand.
box-jump-multiple-response: Continuous/repeated-jump variation carries higher reactive-strength demand and fatigue cost than a single box jump, hence the tighter rep ceiling given cumulative landing-impact loading.
box-squat-with-bands: Bands add accommodating resistance for rate-of-force-development/dynamic-effort work — scored as speed-strength rather than pure max-load strength, with lower hypertrophy value than a straight box squat given the lighter effective bottom-range load.
box-squat-with-chains: Chains deload at the bottom and load up at lockout (accommodating resistance) for dynamic-effort work, same rationale as the banded variant — scored below straight box squat for hypertrophy.
bradford-rocky-presses: Behind-the-neck/partial-ROM press pattern carries elevated shoulder-impingement risk even with good form; strength scored modestly since the movement deliberately avoids lockout and is usually done with submaximal loads.
burpee: Full-body ballistic transitions (squat-plank-pushup-jump) load knees, shoulders, and wrists in sequence, hence multiple joint flags despite good form.
cable-bayesian-curl: Deliberately lengthened-position curl variant (leaning forward, shoulder extended behind torso) directly aligned with the stretch-mediated hypertrophy literature, so hypertrophy is scored above a standard cable curl.
cable-deadlifts: Cable-based hinge loading is inherently lighter than a barbell deadlift, so scored below barbell deadlift variants for strength/fatigue_cost despite sharing the hinge pattern and lower-back stress profile.
cable-glute-kickback-station: Standing kickbacks commonly involve some lumbar hyperextension to complete the rep in typical (not best-case coached) execution, so lower_back is flagged.
cable-hammer-curls-rope-attachment: Duplicate catalog entry — identical name/movement to cable-hammer-curl.
cable-incline-pushdown: Interpreted as a straight-arm lat-pulldown-style isolation movement based on the 'lats' primary-muscle tag, which is unusual for the 'pushdown' name (normally a triceps movement).
cable-incline-triceps-extension: Incline positioning is read as placing the arm in an overhead-type path, so shoulder is flagged alongside elbow, consistent with the other overhead triceps-extension entries.
cable-internal-rotation: Light rotator-cuff/shoulder-health isolation movement, not a hypertrophy or strength-building exercise despite the 'compound' category tag — scored accordingly low across lifting goals.
cable-iron-cross: Wide-arm deep-stretch fly variation with a higher shoulder-stress profile than a standard cable fly given the extended 'iron cross' arm position; scored at/below the standard cable fly per the novelty-is-not-value rule.
cable-judo-flip: Rotational cable chop/flip pattern; scored as a controlled core-rotation exercise rather than assuming ballistic/power intent that the name alone doesn't confirm.
cable-kickback: Same standing-kickback lumbar-compensation reasoning as cable-glute-kickback-station.
cable-lateral-raise: Cable version keeps tension on the delt through the bottom/stretched position (unlike a dumbbell lateral raise, which goes slack there), so lengthened_bias is true here.
cable-lying-triceps-extension: Lying/overhead-path arm position is read as placing the long head under stretch, so shoulder is flagged alongside elbow, consistent with the other overhead triceps-extension entries.
cable-pull-through: Cable pull-through is a beginner-friendly hip-hinge teaching tool (favorable resistance vector vs. barbell RDL), so complexity is scored below barbell hinge variants despite the same lengthened-bias/lower-back profile.
cable-row: Cornerstone horizontal pull; unsupported seated posture places moderate stress on the lower back stabilizers.
cable-russian-twist: Rotational loading under resistance stresses the lumbar spine even with good form.
cable-russian-twists: Rotational loading under resistance stresses the lumbar spine even with good form.
cable-seated-lateral-raise: Cable resistance loads the delt in the arm-down (lengthened) position, unlike dumbbell laterals where torque drops near zero at the bottom.
cable-shrug: Cable maintains tension through the fully depressed (lengthened) bottom position, unlike a barbell shrug.
cable-shrugs: Cable maintains tension through the fully depressed (lengthened) bottom position, unlike a barbell shrug.
cable-standing-leg-curl: Hip-neutral standing position doesn't load the hamstring at long length the way seated (hip-flexed) leg curl does per Maeo et al.; reserve lengthened_bias for the seated variant.
cable-upright-row: Combined internal rotation + abduction pattern is a well-documented shoulder impingement risk even with clean technique.
cable-woodchop: Rotational loading under resistance stresses the lumbar spine, especially with speed/momentum.
cable-woodchopper-station: Rotational loading under resistance stresses the lumbar spine, especially with speed/momentum.
calf-machine-shoulder-shrug: Repurposes a calf-raise machine's shoulder pads to load a shrug; duplicates the cornerstone cable/barbell shrug with worse control, so it scores lower despite the same movement pattern.
calf-press: Loaded dorsiflexed bottom position trains calves at long muscle length, consistent with the lengthened-partials hypertrophy literature (Pedrosa et al.).
calf-press-leg-press: Loaded dorsiflexed bottom position trains calves at long muscle length (Pedrosa et al. lengthened-partials line).
calf-press-on-the-leg-press-machine: Loaded dorsiflexed bottom position trains calves at long muscle length (Pedrosa et al. lengthened-partials line).
calf-raise: Loaded dorsiflexed bottom position trains calves at long muscle length (Pedrosa et al. lengthened-partials line).
calf-raise-on-a-dumbbell: Standing on the dumbbell head as a small platform maximizes ankle dorsiflexion depth, an even deeper stretch position than standard calf-raise variants.
calf-raises-with-bands: Trains calves through the full dorsiflexed stretch position (Pedrosa long-length-partials line), but band tension gives a much lower overload ceiling than a machine.
car-deadlift: Strongman-implement deadlift variant requiring a specialized rig; awkward/shifting load is higher-skill and higher-risk than a standard barbell deadlift.
carioca-quick-step: Agility/footwork drill, not a loaded resistance exercise or true cardio modality — scored on conditioning/movement-quality value; rep window doesn't apply (distance/time-based).
chain-press: Chains reduce resistance at the bottom (stretched) position and add resistance near lockout — the inverse of lengthened-bias loading; an advanced accommodating-resistance tool, not a novice movement.
chair-squat: Bodyweight sit-to-stand squat regression/on-ramp movement — low overload headroom, scored as a beginner progression rather than a strength prescription.
chest-dip: Deep bottom position loads chest/shoulders at long muscle length — a well-cited stretch-emphasis press, though this also elevates anterior shoulder stress.
chest-push-multiple-response: Reactive/rebounding throw variant programmed for repeated explosive reps rather than a single max-effort throw, hence the higher rep window and fatigue cost than the single-response version.

chest-supported-rear-delt-raise: Support eliminates torso momentum and axial/lower-back demand versus a standard bent-over rear-delt raise, making this one of the stricter, higher-quality rear-delt isolation variants.

chin-up: Full dead-hang ROM loads the lats/biceps at long muscle length at the bottom position.
circus-bell: Niche strongman implement (off-axis lever/pendulum overhead lift) — high skill demand and injury risk from awkward loading; not available in typical commercial gyms.
clean-and-jerk: Full competitive Olympic lift (clean + jerk) — highest technical and fatigue demand in the catalog; requires dedicated coaching before loading meaningfully.
clean-deadlift: Deadlift pulled with clean grip/stance as a weightlifting assistance pull — lacks the explosive triple-extension and catch of a full clean, so scored as a strength pull, not a power movement.
clean-from-blocks: Reduced-ROM clean variant starting from blocks — removes the floor pull's technical demand, allowing heavier overload than a full clean, hence scored slightly less complex.
close-grip-push-up-off-of-a-dumbbell: Elevating one hand on a dumbbell adds a deficit stretch at the bottom -- same lengthened-bias logic as deficit pressing work.
conan-s-wheel: Strongman carry dosed by distance/trips rather than reps; heavy full-body axial load comparable to a heavy deadlift variant.
concentration-curl-machine: Assumed bilateral simultaneous machine design; the free-weight version is inherently unilateral (one arm at a time).
copenhagen-plank: Real biomechanical demand is adductor loading at a deep stretch (catalogued here under obliques/core); typically prescribed as a timed hold, not reps.
cross-over-with-bands: Band tension peaks at full contraction, not the stretch -- the opposite resistance curve from a cable or dumbbell fly.
crossbody-cable-triceps-extension: Cross-body path stretches the triceps long head at end range -- lengthened-bias isolation work.
crossover-reverse-lunge: Catalogued as mobility but is a dynamic, loadable lunge pattern -- scored modestly rather than zeroed like a static stretch.
crucifix: Isometric lateral hold, not rep-based -- dosed by hold time (e.g. 15-30s), not reps.
cuban-press: Three-part combination movement (upright row + external rotation + press) -- technical demand exceeds a standard press despite the light loads typically used.
dancer-s-stretch: Pure static stretch -- scored near-zero on lifting goals per rubric; reps are not applicable (time-based hold), so 0/0 like a cardio entry.
db-calf-raise: Standing on the dumbbell adds a deficit -- heel drops below toe line, loading the calf at long length.
db-shoulder-press: Scored as standing overhead work (heavier axial load per rubric); if performed seated with back support, spinal load would be lower.
db-tricep-kickback: Resistance is weakest exactly at lockout (peak contraction) -- notoriously poor overload ceiling despite being a popular isolation move.
dead-hang: Passive/active hang, not rep-based -- dosed by hold time; spine is in traction here, not compression.
deadlift-with-bands: Bands de-load the bottom stretch and add tension toward lockout -- reduces hypertrophy value versus straight weight; commonly used for velocity-intent dynamic-effort work (scored non-explosive by default since intent isn't specified).
deadlift-with-chains: Chains add load progressively toward lockout -- similar accommodating-resistance profile to banded pulls.
decline-close-grip-bench-to-skull-crushe: Skull-crusher phase loads the triceps long head at a deep stretch; the press-to-extension combo is technical and elbow-stressful.
decline-dumbbell-flyes: Catalog tags this 'compound' but it is a fly (isolation) movement identical to Decline Dumbbell Fly; scored on the actual movement pattern.
decline-sit-up: Decline sit-ups add resistance through a fixed spinal-flexion pattern that concentrates load on the lumbar spine.
deficit-deadlift: Deficit stance increases ROM and hamstring/glute stretch loading vs. a standard deadlift (deficit-work lengthened-bias line), but caps achievable load and adds technical demand.
donkey-calf-raise: Deep-stretch calf position; a strong lengthened-bias exemplar (Maeo/Pedrosa evidence line).
donkey-calf-raises: Free-standing bent-over variant (no machine support) shifts some load onto the lower back versus the machine version.
double-kettlebell-alternating-hang-clean: Each rep cleans one bell at a time (alternating), so scored unilateral despite using two kettlebells.
double-kettlebell-snatch: Double-kettlebell snatch is a high-skill, high-fatigue ballistic movement; complexity scored at the top of the scale per the snatch-family anchor.
double-kettlebell-windmill: Double-KB windmill is a niche, high-skill stability/mobility movement; complexity capped at the top of the scale, not a volume-hypertrophy tool.
double-leg-butt-kick: Two-footed jump/plyo drill (heel-to-glute), not a low-impact cyclical warm-up variant; scored as plyometric conditioning work.
dragon-flag: Elite-tier bodyweight core skill move; complexity capped at the top of the scale, most users need a regression.
drop-push: Plyometric/explosive push variant; scored as a power movement, not a strength-hypertrophy press.
dumbbell-floor-press: Reduced ROM (elbows contact floor) shortens the stretch position, so not a lengthened-bias movement; generally easier on the shoulder than a standard bench press.
dumbbell-prone-incline-curl: Steep-incline prone position maximizes biceps stretch under load; a strong lengthened-bias exemplar, high hypertrophy value.
dumbbell-pullover: Behind-head arm position loads lats/chest at long length; treated as a lengthened-bias movement despite lighter typical loading.
dumbbell-raise: Generic 'raise' name and single-joint movement pattern; scored as a shoulder isolation raise despite the 'compound' catalog tag.
dumbbell-seated-box-jump: Loaded (dumbbell) box jump from a seated dead stop is a high-risk, high-skill power movement; complexity and joint stress scored at the top of scale, reps capped very low.
dumbbell-side-bend: Loaded lateral flexion under standing axial load is flagged for lower-back stress; conservative rep ceiling.
dumbbell-squat-to-a-bench: Bench provides a depth cue/regression, reducing technical demand versus a free dumbbell squat.
dumbbell-upright-row: Narrow-grip pull into internal rotation/abduction is a well-known shoulder-impingement risk; keep loads moderate.
elevated-back-lunge: Single-leg barbell lunge from an elevated stance combines loaded balance with axial spine load — score as a Bulgarian-split-squat-tier movement.
exercise-ball-crunch: Ball's curvature extends the spine at the bottom, giving abs more stretch under tension than a floor crunch.
external-rotation: Rotator-cuff prehab isolation; light/high-rep by design, not a loadable mass builder.
external-rotation-with-band: Source data tags this 'compound' but it is a single-joint rotator-cuff isolation move; scored on true demand.
ez-bar-preacher-curl: Strict stretch-position biceps loading; more distal-tendon/elbow stress than a standing curl.
ez-bar-skullcrusher: Well-documented elbow-tendon stress at the bottom stretch position; common source of elbow tendinopathy if overused.
farmer-s-walk: Distance/time-based loaded carry, not a rep-based lift (rep fields not applicable, set to 0/0).
farmers-carry: Same movement as Farmer's Walk; distance/time-based, not rep-based.
fast-skipping: Tagged 'compound' but functions as a plyometric conditioning drill; impact and leg-interference scored on the actual movement.
finger-curls: Deliberately rolls the load into the fingertips for a lengthened wrist-flexor position.
flat-bench-lying-leg-raise: Straight-leg raise pattern is a common lower-back stress point if the lumbar spine isn't braced.
flexor-incline-dumbbell-curls: Arm hangs behind the torso on the incline, stretching the biceps under load at the bottom.
floor-glute-ham-raise: Nordic-curl-family eccentric hamstring work — well-evidenced for injury prevention, but most untrained lifters cannot complete a full rep.
floor-press: Floor contact truncates ROM at the bottom, removing the stretch position — good for triceps lockout, not a stretch-hypertrophy exercise.
floor-press-with-chains: Accommodating-resistance dynamic-effort tool for advanced lifters, not a hypertrophy movement.
flutter-kicks: Core/hip-flexor endurance move; commonly flagged for lower-back strain under fatigue with poor pelvic bracing.
forearm-roller-machine: Prescription window is roll-up-and-down cycles, not conventional reps.
forward-drag-with-press: Sled-drag-plus-press complex is distance-based, not rep-based; strong conditioning/calorie tool, low true strength-overload ceiling.
frankenstein-squat: Arms-extended position removes rack support and caps achievable load well below a standard front squat — a technique/coaching tool, not a max-strength builder.
frog-hops: Tagged 'mobility' but is a bodyweight hopping/plyometric drill; impact and leg-interference scored on the actual movement.
frog-sit-ups: Repeated spinal flexion under load; sit-up-family movements are commonly flagged for lower-back disc stress at high rep counts.
front-barbell-squat-to-a-bench: Bench depth cue reduces the balance/depth-judgment demand slightly versus a free front squat.
front-incline-dumbbell-raise: Incline angle shifts resistance to load the front delt in a more stretched position than a standing raise.
front-raise: Appears to duplicate the standard dumbbell front raise entry (slug dumbbell-front-raise) — scored identically.
front-raise-and-pullover: Old-school straight-arm combo; the pullover phase loads lats/chest overhead at long length with a long lever arm on the shoulder.
front-squat-clean-grip: Fingertip clean-grip rack demands more wrist/shoulder mobility than the cross-arm front-squat grip and often limits reps via grip fatigue.
full-range-of-motion-lat-pulldown: Name explicitly emphasizes full stretch-to-contraction ROM versus a standard partial-ROM pulldown.
gironda-sternum-chins: Advanced lean-back sternum chin-up variant; most lifters cannot execute the full elbows-back path without significant practice.
glute-bridge-machine: Machine loading takes this well beyond bodyweight glute-bridge capacity for hypertrophy/strength.
glute-ham-developer: GHD/GHR loads hamstrings eccentrically at long muscle length (Nordic-curl-family evidence); external load ceiling limited so strength capped below barbell hinges.
glute-kickback: Bodyweight donkey-kick pattern; low load ceiling keeps it an activation/accessory move, not a strength builder.
glute-kickback-machine: Loaded machine version starts from hip flexion (stretched glute) under real resistance, unlike the bodyweight kickback.
goblet-squat: Front-loaded hold caps how heavy it can go, so it functions as a squat-pattern teaching regression rather than a max-strength tool.

ground-base-combo-twist: Standing loaded rotation; flagged for lower back given axial+rotational load under resistance.
guillotine-bench-press: Neck-level bar path with flared elbows gives a deeper pec stretch but is the signature high-risk bench variation for anterior shoulder stress; narrower rep window is deliberately conservative.

handstand-push-ups: Elite bodyweight skill (inverted overhead press); high complexity/joint-stress and low rep ceiling make it unsuitable for circuits despite being 'bodyweight'.

hang-snatch: Most technical barbell lift in the catalog; lighter absolute loads than clean variants further limit hypertrophy value, and the fragile overhead catch makes coaches more cautious using it in fatigued conditioning circuits.
hanging-leg-raise-station: Back/forearm-supported station removes the grip/shoulder-hang demand of the free-hanging variant, hence lower complexity and no flagged joint stress.
heaving-snatch-balance: Specialized Olympic-weightlifting technique drill (speed-under-the-bar into an overhead squat catch), not a general strength/hypertrophy/conditioning tool; low focus scores despite explosive=true and top-tier complexity are intentional.
heavy-bag-thrust: Best classified as a combat-conditioning drill (explosive repeated push against resistance), not a hypertrophy movement, despite the chest/triceps muscle tags.
heel-elevated-goblet-squat: Heel elevation increases achievable knee flexion/quad stretch versus a flat goblet squat, so unlike the flat version this one is lengthened-bias.
high-cable-curls: Arm-behind-torso cable curl loads the biceps long head at a deep stretch (Bayesian-curl pattern) under constant tension.
hip-abduction-machine: Seated abduction machines start with the leg adducted, loading glute medius at a stretched position (seated-leg-curl-style lengthened bias).
hip-adduction-machine: Starts with the leg abducted, loading the adductors at a stretched position under resistance.
hip-extension-with-bands: Band tension is greatest at hip extension (shortened glute), not at the stretched start, so despite the hinge pattern this is an ascending-resistance movement, not lengthened-bias.
hip-flexion-with-band: Same ascending-resistance band profile as hip-extension-with-bands: hardest near the shortened end of the ROM, not the stretch.
hip-lift-with-band: Band around the hips is most stretched (hardest) at hip lockout, the shortened glute position, so this is ascending-resistance rather than lengthened-bias.
hip-thrust-machine: Guided, torso-supported hip-extension pattern is the cornerstone glute hypertrophy movement (Contreras EMG line), with real stretch-position glute loading at the bottom.
hollow-body-hold: Isometric time-under-tension hold, not a discrete-rep movement, so rep_min/rep_max are 0/0 by the same logic as the cardio carve-out rather than an invented rep count.
hurdle-hops: Bodyweight jump/plyometric work: high impact and true leg-interference risk (Wilson line) if programmed near heavy squat/deadlift sessions in the same window.
hyperextensions-with-no-hyperextension-b: Floor substitute without a bench to hang the torso over the pad, so it can't load the erectors/hamstrings at the same lengthened starting stretch as the true hyperextension-bench version; lower ceiling on load and hypertrophy stimulus follow.
inchworm: Dynamic warm-up drill, not a training stimulus; reps reflect common warm-up prescription even though training-goal value is nil.
incline-barbell-triceps-extension: Incline angle puts the upper arm in an overhead-like position at the bottom, loading triceps at long length similar to overhead extension.
incline-bench-pull: Chest-supported barbell row; scored as a compound back movement despite the catalog's isolation tag.
incline-db-curl: Shoulder-extended incline position stretches the long head of biceps at the bottom (classic lengthened-bias curl).
incline-db-row: Chest-supported on the incline bench, so lower-back stress typical of bent-over rows is minimal.
incline-dumbbell-bench-with-palms-facing: Neutral (palms-in) grip reduces the anterior shoulder stress typical of incline pressing.
incline-dumbbell-curl: Shoulder-extended incline position stretches the long head of biceps at the bottom (classic lengthened-bias curl).
incline-dumbbell-flyes-with-a-twist: Adds a wrist-rotation component to the standard fly, slightly higher skill demand.
incline-hammer-curls: Neutral grip shifts emphasis to brachialis/brachioradialis; incline position still stretches the flexors at the bottom.
incline-machine-fly: Fixed machine arc still stretches the chest at the start position; guided path limits stress relative to free-weight flyes.
incline-push-up: Bodyweight regression (elevated hands reduce load); on-ramp toward flat push-ups/pressing, not a strength cornerstone.
incline-push-up-close-grip: Close hand spacing increases elbow/triceps-tendon loading versus standard push-up width.
incline-push-up-depth-jump: Plyometric push-up; kept to low reps for power quality, flagged explosive for circuit/conditioning slotting.
incline-push-up-reverse-grip: Reverse hand orientation increases wrist positioning demand versus standard push-up grip.
incline-push-up-wide: Wide hand spacing increases shoulder horizontal-abduction stress at the bottom.
intermediate-hip-flexor-and-quad-stretch: Kneeling lunge-style stretch performed one side at a time.
internal-rotation-with-band: Light rotator-cuff/rehab isolation work, not a hypertrophy or strength driver.
iron-cross: Niche floor-based rotational stability drill (arms held wide with light dumbbells while legs rotate); scored as a low-load stability movement, not a strength/hypertrophy cornerstone.
iso-lateral-ab-crunch: Loaded spinal flexion under resistance; kept off very low reps to limit lumbar disc stress.
iso-lateral-behind-neck-press: Behind-the-neck path demands more shoulder external rotation/range than a front press; kept off very low reps and flagged for shoulder-limited users.
iso-lateral-calf-press: Bottom position allows a deep ankle dorsiflexion stretch, analogous to deficit calf-raise work in the length-emphasis literature.
iso-lateral-chest-supported-row: Chest pad eliminates the lower-back involvement typical of free-weight bent-over rows.
iso-lateral-deadlift: Guided hip-hinge path lowers technical demand versus a free deadlift, but the pattern still loads the posterior chain/spine heavily, so fatigue and spinal load stay near free-deadlift levels.
iso-lateral-glute-drive: Hip-thrust pattern; lumbar can hyperextend at lockout under heavy load.
iso-lateral-hack-squat: Back pad reduces axial spinal loading versus a free back squat, but the fixed path concentrates compressive stress at the knee, especially deep.
iso-lateral-leg-curl: Catalog name doesn't confirm seated vs. prone; scored as the more common prone/lying design rather than assuming the deeper-stretch seated variant.
iso-lateral-leg-press: Well supported, but excessive depth under heavy load is a known cause of posterior pelvic tilt/lower-back strain, so lower_back is flagged alongside knee.
iso-lateral-pec-fly: Wide-arm start position stretches the pecs similar to a dumbbell fly, within a machine-guided, lower-risk path.
iso-lateral-preacher-curl: Preacher position stretches biceps at the bottom of the rep, similar to the incline-curl lengthened-bias mechanism.
iso-lateral-pulldown-machine-alternating: Alternating arms adds anti-rotation core demand and unilateral loading vs. standard bilateral pulldown.
iso-lateral-pullover-machine: Overhead arc loads lats at long length — classic lengthened-bias pattern.
iso-lateral-rear-delt-fly: Fly pattern loads rear delts at a lengthened position.
iso-lateral-torso-rotation: Loaded spinal rotation carries lumbar shear stress even seated/supported; keep loads moderate.
iso-lateral-underhand-pulldown: Underhand grip shifts load toward biceps/elbow flexors vs. standard pulldown.
isometric-chest-squeezes: Low-load isometric activation drill, not a progressive-overload chest movement.
isometric-wipers: Chest tagged as primary but movement is a plank-based anti-rotation hold — scored as a core/stability drill.
it-band-and-glute-stretch: Mobility/stretch work scores ~0 across lifting goals; reps n/a (dosed by hold-time).
jackknife-sit-up: Repeated loaded lumbar flexion; flag lower back despite no axial spinal load.
jammer-press: Standing plate-loaded press station; some drive from legs so light axial load.
janda-sit-up: Heel-drive technique reduces hip-flexor contribution but trunk flexion still loads lower back.
jefferson-squats: Asymmetric straddle stance creates spinal torque/shear beyond a standard back squat — high skill, low reps.
jerk-balance: Olympic-lifting positional/balance drill (split-stance overhead receiving position), not a hypertrophy movement.
jerk-dip-squat: Fast, shallow dip trains explosive leg drive for the jerk — velocity-intent, not a hypertrophy squat variant.
jm-press: Hybrid close-grip bench/skull-crusher; heavy triceps-dominant press with real elbow-tendon stress.
jogging-treadmill: Repeated ground-impact loading through an upright spine warrants moderate (not zero) spinal_load.
jump-squat: Bodyweight-only caps strength/hypertrophy value; plyometric landing impact drives fatigue and knee stress despite no external load.
keg-load: Strongman-style odd-object ground-to-platform lift; heavy axial/lower-back demand comparable to deadlift variants.
kettlebell-dead-clean: Dead-stop start (no backswing) removes momentum assistance, closer to a strength pull than touch-and-go — lower rep ceiling.
kettlebell-figure-8: Light-load coordination/warm-up drill, not a loading movement for strength or hypertrophy.
kettlebell-front-rack-carry: Loaded carry — normally dosed by distance/time; reps shown as an approximate step-count window.
kettlebell-halo: Light-load shoulder mobility/warm-up drill, not a loading movement.
kettlebell-one-legged-deadlift: Single-leg hip hinge stretches the hamstring under load at the bottom — lengthened-bias stimulus; balance limits loading.
kettlebell-pirate-ships: Lateral-flexion core/shoulder stabilization drill; moderate lateral spinal loading.
kettlebell-pistol-squat: Extreme balance/mobility/strength demand for a single-leg loaded squat — treat as an advanced skill movement; low reps.
kettlebell-seesaw-press: Alternating single-arm overhead press; anti-lateral-flexion core/lower-back demand from asymmetric loading.
kettlebell-shoulder-press: Core listed as secondary muscle implies the single-arm variant with anti-lateral-flexion demand.
kettlebell-sumo-high-pull: Explosive hip-driven pull to chest height — power-intent movement akin to the clean family.
kettlebell-thruster: Squat-to-overhead-press combo; explosive leg drive carries into the press, hits axial load twice (squat + lockout).
kettlebell-turkish-get-up-lunge-style: Multi-stage floor-to-stand sequence with sustained overhead lockout — among the highest-skill loaded movements; very low reps by design.
kettlebell-turkish-get-up-squat-style: Squat-style transition variant of the Turkish get-up — same high-skill, low-rep profile as the lunge-style version.
kettlebell-windmill: Overhead lateral hinge stretches obliques/lats under load; shoulder stability plus hip mobility combined — advanced movement.
kipping-muscle-up: Kipping (momentum-assisted) reduces pure strength/hypertrophy stimulus vs. a strict muscle-up; extremely high skill regardless.
knee-across-the-body: Mobility/stretch work scores ~0 across lifting goals; reps n/a (dosed by hold-time).
knee-circles: Mobility/warm-up drill scores ~0 across lifting goals; reps n/a (dosed by hold-time).
kneeling-arm-drill: Sprint-mechanics technique drill, not a loaded strength/conditioning movement -- scored near-zero on lifting goals.
kneeling-cable-triceps-extension: Assumed overhead-angle cable variant (kneeling stance implies reaching overhead/behind head), so triceps load at long muscle length -- lengthened-bias true.
kneeling-jump-squat: Barbell-loaded explosive kneeling-to-squat jump -- treated as a loaded jump/power movement with axial spinal load and landing impact.
kneeling-leg-curl: Kneeling/standing leg curls train hamstrings from a hip-neutral position (unlike the classic hip-flexed seated leg curl), so lengthened-bias is scored false; machine loads one leg at a time.
kroc-row: High-rep, momentum-assisted heavy DB row -- strong strength/hypertrophy stimulus but real lower-back load from the body-English technique.
l-sit: Isometric gymnastic hold; rep_min/max approximated as hold-attempts since prescription is normally time-based (~15-45s holds).
landmine-180: Rotational landmine pivot drill typically performed with dynamic intent -- scored as a rotational power/conditioning movement, not a strength builder.
landmine-180-s: Duplicate catalog entry for the same landmine 180 movement; scored identically.
landmine-linear-jammer: Full-body explosive press-drive pattern (combine-style landmine jammer) -- high conditioning/explosive value, low direct hypertrophy/strength specificity.
lateral-raise-machine-plate-loaded-iso-l: Plate-loaded iso-lateral design allows heavier loading and per-side control than a pin-stack lateral raise machine.
lateral-raise-with-bands: Band resistance curve (light at bottom, heaviest at top) makes very low reps impractical -- rep floor raised vs free-weight lateral raise.
leg-curl: Assumed prone/lying variant (hip-neutral) given the unqualified name -- hamstrings aren't loaded at the long length a seated leg curl achieves, so lengthened-bias is false.
leg-over-floor-press: Floor press with a leg raised for anti-rotation core demand -- likely single-arm/single-KB execution, so scored unilateral with higher complexity than a standard floor press.
leg-press-calf-press: Leg-press platform allows a deep ankle-dorsiflexion stretch under load, matching the deficit/stretch-emphasis lengthened-bias pattern.
leg-press-calf-raise: Same mechanism as leg-press calf press -- deep stretch under load at the bottom position.
leverage-deadlift: Machine-guided hinge pattern still transmits substantial axial/lower-back load despite the fixed bar path, so spinal_load and rep ceiling are scored like a free deadlift even though complexity is much lower.
linear-3-part-start-technique: Track & field sprint-start technique drill -- scored as conditioning/speed work, not a lifting movement; strength/hypertrophy near zero.
linear-acceleration-wall-drill: Wall-supported sprint-mechanics drill -- much lower ground-reaction/impact than free sprint-start work, so scored lower on impact/interference/fatigue than the unsupported start-technique drill.
linear-depth-jump: High-intensity reactive plyometric with real injury risk/technical demand -- among the most advanced jump-training movements in the catalog.
log-lift: Strongman ground-to-overhead lift with a bulky implement -- near-max complexity, fatigue, and spinal load; explosive clean phase into an overhead lockout.
london-bridges: Uncommon back-pulling movement (name/equipment tag suggest a rings or suspension-trainer pull) -- scored with moderate-high complexity given limited standardization of technique.
low-cable-crossover: Low-to-high cable fly loads the chest through a stretched position -- matches the rubric's 'flys with stretch emphasis' lengthened-bias example.
low-cable-triceps-extension: Assumed low-pulley overhead-style path (arm extends overhead behind head), matching the rubric's overhead-extension lengthened-bias example.
low-pulley-row-to-neck: Upright-row-pattern pull to neck; flagged for shoulder impingement risk at end range.
lower-back-curl: Mobility drill scored ~0 on lifting goals per rubric convention; interpreted as a repeated flexion movement (not a static hold), hence a real rep window rather than 0/0.
lower-back-smr: Static hold; rep window n/a (0/0, extending the cardio convention). Rolling directly over the lumbar spine (vs. paraspinal muscle) is a commonly cited caution, hence lower_back flag.
lunge-pass-through: Complexity scored 4 (not 2-3) due to the unilateral balance + hand-to-hand pass-through coordination demand.
lunge-sprint: Interpreted 'sprint' as signaling explosive/power tempo given ambiguous naming (machine equipment, lunge pattern, no jump/plyo indicated) rather than literal running.
lying-bent-leg-groin: Static stretch; rep window n/a (0/0, extending the cardio convention).
lying-cable-curl: Lying cable curl loads biceps with the shoulder extended behind the torso -- a stretched start position, hence lengthened_bias true.
lying-close-grip-bar-curl-on-high-pulley: High-pulley path stretches biceps at the bottom (shoulder extended) -- same stretch-position logic as other lying cable curl variants.
lying-close-grip-barbell-triceps-extensi: Behind-the-head path loads triceps at a deep stretch; flagged elbow (and end-range shoulder) strain risk -- coach load conservatively.
lying-close-grip-barbell-triceps-press-t: To-chin variant is a shorter, more lockout-biased ROM than the behind-the-head version, so scored lengthened_bias false despite being in the same family.
lying-crossover: Interpreted as a dynamic repeated rotation (not a static hold), hence a real rep window rather than 0/0.
lying-dumbbell-tricep-extension: Duplicate catalog entry for the same movement as lying-db-tricep-extension (differs only in tagged secondary muscles); scored identically.
lying-face-down-plate-neck-resistance: Cervical spine is directly loaded in flexion under external resistance; flagged spinal_load=1 even though the fixed joint_stress list has no neck option.
lying-face-up-plate-neck-resistance: Cervical spine is directly loaded in extension under external resistance; flagged spinal_load=1 even though the fixed joint_stress list has no neck option.
lying-glute: Static stretch; rep window n/a (0/0, extending the cardio convention).
lying-hamstring: Static stretch; rep window n/a (0/0, extending the cardio convention).
lying-leg-curl: Lying/prone leg curl is the non-lengthened-bias hamstring curl variant (hip stays extended) -- contrast with seated leg curl, which the rubric flags as the lengthened-bias version.
lying-leg-curl-machine: Same lying/prone leg-curl pattern as lying-leg-curl; not the lengthened-bias (seated) variant.
lying-leg-curls: Same lying/prone leg-curl pattern as lying-leg-curl; not the lengthened-bias (seated) variant.
lying-leg-raise: Straight-leg raise pattern commonly loads the lumbar spine via anterior pelvic tilt if hip flexors dominate over abs -- flagged lower_back.
lying-prone-quadriceps: Static stretch; rep window n/a (0/0, extending the cardio convention).
lying-supine-dumbbell-curl: Supine position extends the shoulder behind the torso, stretching the biceps at the bottom -- same logic as other lying curl variants.
lying-triceps-press: Standard EZ-bar skull-crusher path stretches triceps well at the bottom of the rep.
machine-dip: Assumed a loaded lever/plate-loaded dip station (not an assisted-dip machine) since 'assisted' isn't in the name; scores reflect a real compound press, not an on-ramp regression.
machine-hip-thrust: Spinal load kept low (0) despite heavy hip-hinge loading -- torso is bench-supported throughout, a key advantage of hip thrust vs. free-weight hinge variants (Contreras/Vigotsky glute-EMG literature).
machine-preacher-curl: Preacher curl scored lengthened_bias=false -- the pad limits shoulder extension at the bottom, so it doesn't reach the long-length stretch that lying/incline curl variants do.
machine-pullover: Machine pullover stretches the lats overhead at the top of the rep -- a classic lengthened-bias exercise.
machine-shoulder-press: Duplicate catalog entry for the same movement as machine-shoulder-military-press; scored identically.
machine-triceps-extension: Duplicate catalog entry for the same movement as machine-tricep-extension; scored identically.
meadows-row: Landmine unilateral row allows a deep bottom-position lat stretch (frequently cited as the exercise's signature trait) -- hence lengthened_bias true; asymmetric bent-over loading also flagged for lower-back stress.
middle-back-shrug: Standing loaded shrug scored spinal_load=1 (static axial hold), though load is typically light-moderate relative to squat/deadlift.
middle-back-stretch: Static stretch; rep window n/a (0/0, extending the cardio convention).
mixed-grip-chin: Mixed-grip (asymmetric hand orientation) flagged for added, uneven shoulder/elbow stress vs. a standard pull-up.
mountain-climber: Impact scored 'none' (not 'low') since ground contact is via a supported plank rather than weight-bearing gait; not explosive since it's conditioning-tempo, not max-velocity intent.
moving-claw-series: Name/metadata don't map to a standard named lift; scored conservatively as a niche hamstring-focus assistance movement, not a cornerstone.
multi-hip-machine-extension-setting: Single-leg machine starting from hip flexion loads the glute at long length through extension.
multi-hip-machine-trunk-rotation: Resisted trunk rotation loads the lumbar spine in torsion; keep loads conservative.
narrow-stance-squat: Narrow stance shifts more load onto quads/knees relative to conventional-stance squats.
narrow-stance-squats: Narrow stance shifts more load onto quads/knees relative to conventional-stance squats.
natural-glute-ham-raise: Bodyweight hamstring exercise loaded heavily at long muscle length (GHR/Nordic line of evidence); very hard for most trainees without assistance.
neck-press: Bar path to the neck ('guillotine press') carries meaningful shoulder-impingement/instability risk; most coaches program it cautiously.
nordic-curl-bench: Canonical lengthened-position hamstring exercise (Nordic/GHR evidence line); most trainees cannot complete full-ROM reps unassisted.
nordic-hamstring-curl: Canonical lengthened-position hamstring exercise (Nordic/GHR evidence line); most trainees cannot complete full-ROM reps unassisted.
oblique-crunch-machine: Machine is loaded and worked one side per set (like the multi-hip machine), unlike bodyweight oblique crunches which alternate within a set.
olympic-squat: High-bar/deep squat style typical of weightlifting; scored as a standard barbell squat pattern.
one-arm-chin-up: Elite-rarity skill with essentially no practical overload headroom for most trainees, despite the high raw force requirement; scored low on prescribable training value.
one-arm-floor-press: Floor contact shortens the ROM (no bottom stretch) and single-arm barbell control is unusually demanding for stability.
one-arm-high-pulley-cable-side-bends: Loaded lateral spinal flexion; keep loads moderate given lumbar shear/disc concerns with heavy side bends.
one-arm-incline-lateral-raise: Incline angle preserves tension through the stretched/bottom position of the delt, unlike a standing lateral raise.
one-arm-kettlebell-para-press: Typically performed kneeling/seated (stability-focused), not standing, so scored lower on spinal_load than a standing overhead press.
one-arm-kettlebell-split-jerk: Split footwork under fatigue is a real injury-risk factor, scored below the standard clean/jerk for circuit/conditioning suitability.
one-arm-kettlebell-split-snatch: Split footwork under fatigue is a real injury-risk factor, scored below the standard snatch for circuit/conditioning suitability.
one-arm-long-bar-row: One-handed control of a long/anchored bar is meaningfully less stable than a dumbbell row.
one-arm-overhead-kettlebell-squats: Extreme stability/mobility demand (overhead + single-arm + squat); loads used are typically far lighter than standard squats.
one-arm-pronated-dumbbell-triceps-extens: Grip/position variant of isolated triceps extension; scored as standard triceps isolation given ambiguous exact form from the name alone.
one-arm-side-deadlift: Offset/suitcase-style loaded hinge with heavy anti-lateral-flexion core demand; achievable load is lower than a bilateral deadlift due to grip/stability limits.
one-arm-supinated-dumbbell-triceps-exten: Overhead position loads triceps at long length (lengthened-bias).
one-handed-hang: Mobility/decompression hang, not a hypertrophy stimulus despite real grip/shoulder loading.
one-leg-barbell-squat: High-skill unilateral barbell squat; balance limits absolute load vs bilateral squat.
open-palm-kettlebell-clean: Explosive KB pattern; open-palm cue reduces forearm impact vs standard clean.
otis-up: Combines weighted sit-up with overhead hold; notable spinal flexion load.
overhead-cable-curl: Shoulder-extended overhead cable position loads biceps long head at long length (lengthened-bias).
overhead-slam: High-value conditioning/circuit movement; minimal hypertrophy stimulus given brief time under tension.
overhead-squat: Elite mobility/skill demand caps practical load; strength/hypertrophy value below back squat despite similar spinal loading.
overhead-triceps-extension-machine: Machine-guided lengthened-position triceps work; matches overhead-extension pattern.
pallof-press-with-rotation: Adds controlled trunk rotation under load vs. static Pallof press; flagged for lower-back rotational stress.
pec-deck-fly: Handle-based fly machine likely allows deeper stretch ROM than pad-style pec deck (inferred from movement_pattern tag).
pendlay-row: Dead-stop pull built for bar speed, but heavy barbell loading makes it unsuitable for circuit slots -- not flagged explosive.
pendulum-squat: Arc path maintains quad tension in deep flexion (lengthened-bias); back-supported, minimal spinal load.
pendulum-squat-machine: Appears to duplicate the Pendulum Squat entry (same machine/pattern); scored identically.
pin-presses: Partial-ROM overload tool for strength/sticking-point work; less hypertrophy value than full-ROM press due to truncated ROM.
pistol-squat: Elite bodyweight balance/mobility demand; strength ceiling capped without external load.
plank: Isometric hold; scored as bodyweight time-based exercise (rep range n/a).
plate-loaded-deadlift-machine: Machine-guided hinge pattern; still heavy axial/posterior-chain load despite support.
plate-loaded-shoulder-press-machine: Seated/supported machine -- no axial spinal load unlike standing barbell overhead press.
plate-pinch: Isometric grip/pinch hold; scored as time-based (rep range n/a).
plate-twist: Loaded spinal rotation; flagged for lower-back stress (combined flexion+rotation+load).
platform-hamstring-slides: Bridge-position slider curl keeps hip extended, so not a lengthened-position hamstring exercise like seated leg curl.
plyo-kettlebell-pushups: Plyometric push-up on KB handles adds balance/wrist-stability demand vs standard plyo push-up.
power-clean: Olympic-lift-family movement; high strength/power value, moderate hypertrophy due to brief loaded time-under-tension.
power-clean-from-blocks: From-blocks variant shortens the pull (removes floor-to-knee phase), reducing technical demand and hypertrophy time-under-tension vs standard power clean.
power-jerk: Overhead Olympic-lift catch; heavy axial + overhead load, minimal hypertrophy value given brief time-under-tension.
power-partials: Partial top-range shoulder isolation despite 'power' naming; not a ballistic full-body movement, so not flagged explosive.
power-snatch: Most technically demanding barbell lift; overhead catch + heavy pull combine wrist/shoulder/lower-back stress.
power-snatch-from-blocks: From-blocks variant shortens the pull, reducing technical/ROM demand slightly vs standard power snatch.
power-stairs: Bodyweight explosive stair-climbing conditioning drill; high impact loading competes with heavy leg training.
preacher-hammer-dumbbell-curl: Preacher angle biases the stretched position at full elbow extension.
press-sit-up: Loaded spinal flexion combined with an overhead press adds low-back and shoulder stress beyond a standard sit-up.
prone-manual-hamstring: Partner-applied manual resistance lacks progressive-overload precision, capping strength/hypertrophy value versus machine leg curls.
prowler-sprint: Concentric-only push mechanics (no eccentric braking) keep true leg-day interference low despite high conditioning/calorie demand; sled work is explicitly power-intent.
pull-through: Cable hip hinge loads glutes/hamstrings at long length through the bottom range.
pull-up: Full dead-hang bottom position loads the lats near end-range length each rep.
pullover-machine: Classic long-length lat loading with arms overhead.
push-press-behind-the-neck: Behind-the-neck bar path demands unusual shoulder external-rotation/thoracic mobility and carries elevated impingement risk versus a standard push press.
push-up-to-side-plank: Rotational side-plank finish adds a unilateral anti-rotation core demand beyond a standard push-up.
push-ups-with-feet-elevated: Feet-elevated angle shifts emphasis toward upper chest/shoulders and increases relative loading vs a standard push-up.
push-ups-with-feet-on-an-exercise-ball: Ball-under-feet instability adds a large core-stabilization/skill demand; a novelty variant that scores below the standard push-up on strength/hypertrophy.
pushups-close-and-wide-hand-positions: Alternating hand positions mid-set raises total work capacity and coordination demand vs a single-stance push-up.
pyramid: Static mobility hold; scored near-zero on lifting-goal axes per mobility convention, reps N/A (duration-based).
rack-delivery: Olympic-lift catch/rack-position drill; technical demand and power intent place it near the clean/snatch family.
rack-pull-with-bands: Band tension increasing toward lockout is a classic accommodating-resistance setup for speed-strength work, distinct from a straight rack pull.
rdl: Deep hip-hinge ROM loads hamstrings at long length, a stretch-mediated hypertrophy driver; rep ceiling kept moderate given axial spinal load.
renegade-row: Plank anti-rotation row combo carries meaningful core/low-back stabilization demand and coordination skill beyond a standard row.
reverse-band-bench-press: Band-assisted bottom position allows supramaximal lockout loading; a specialized powerlifting overload tool, not a general cornerstone press.
reverse-band-box-squat: Band-assisted box squat for supramaximal overload/speed work; a specialized powerlifting tool rather than a cornerstone squat pattern.
reverse-band-deadlift: Band-assisted deadlift for supramaximal lockout overload; specialized powerlifting tool.
reverse-band-power-squat: Band-assisted wide-stance squat for supramaximal overload; specialized powerlifting tool.
reverse-band-sumo-deadlift: Band-assisted sumo deadlift for supramaximal lockout overload; specialized powerlifting tool.
reverse-barbell-curl: Pronated grip shifts emphasis to brachioradialis/forearms and increases wrist strain vs a standard curl.
reverse-barbell-preacher-curls: Preacher angle biases the stretched position at full elbow extension; pronated grip adds forearm emphasis.
reverse-flyes-with-external-rotation: Added external-rotation component increases rotator-cuff/shoulder-stabilizer demand and technical complexity vs a standard reverse fly.
reverse-grip-pulldown: Underhand grip with full overhead ROM loads lats/biceps at long length.
reverse-hyperextension: Reverse hyper is traction/decompressive on the spine despite the hip-hinge pattern (a known rehab tool), unlike loaded good mornings; loads glutes/hamstrings at a lengthened hip-flexed bottom position.
reverse-hyperextension-machine: Traction/decompressive on the spine despite the hip-hinge pattern; loads glutes/hamstrings at a lengthened bottom position.
reverse-plate-curls: Niche plate-implement variant of the reverse curl pattern; duplicates the cornerstone movement without added stimulus.
reverse-triceps-bench-press: Underhand-grip bench variant increases wrist/shoulder strain and technical risk vs standard or close-grip bench press.
rhomboids-smr: Self-myofascial release, not a resistance movement; scored near-zero on lifting goals per mobility convention.
rickshaw-carry: Loaded carry; heavy axial per rubric's loaded-carry example. Programmed by distance/time in practice; reps given as attempt-count proxy.
